title: constrain-floor-authors-and-provenance-is-measured
intention: constrain's floor AUTHORS the packet fields that are lookup rather than language — constraints and unknowns — and provenance for them stops being declared by the author and becomes DERIVED from whether the ceiling changed the floor's answer. The enabling primitive, missing until now, is address.component_of: given a PATH, which component owns it.
why:
MEASURED 2026-08-14, and the measurement is of the floor's input rather than its output, which is why it went unseen. constrain's floor tested each of orient's refs for membership in the component ROSTER — a set of bare NAMES. Since orient's floor started grounding its refs the same morning, a ref is a path far more often than a name: 266 of the 310 refs across the 45 berthed orient packets are paths. So the floor DISCARDED 86% of its own input and emitted an empty constraint list. An empty list is a legal list, so nothing redded anywhere in the system.

The consequence is the same shape orient's build closed one rung up, and it lands on the same instrument: 24 of 41 berthed constrain packets declare constraints: floor while the floor produced ZERO charter constraints for that input, and ten more produced exactly one, against ceiling lists running 5 to 19 items across five kinds. The number is a self-report.

THE LIVED SYMPTOM, and it is Akien's: he is deciding what to build next off skills/chart/dial.py. A pass that reports itself compiled when it is producing nothing tells him the cheapest remaining work is elsewhere, and the staircase stalls on a number nobody computed. Under the ruling of the same day the stakes are larger than tidiness — the ceiling for these passes is becoming Hex, and a failover only means anything if the floor's answer is a FACT the next rung can read.
traces_to: Ruling 2026-08-14-the-preamble-compiles-to-learn-not-to-be-cheap — the build order is Akien's: 'starting with orientation, we build out everything we can now ... orientation will add a json packet to the ticket, constrain will add to that. those can be completely deterministic. and ONCE THEY WORK we can start working on the other ones later.'
Law 3 — nothing is known until measured. A provenance the author stamps is an unmeasured claim wearing a measurement's name.

Law 4 — a rule enforced by physics, not policy. 'Label the field honestly' is discipline; deriving the label removes the discretion, and constrain's charter gains gated_by: ['CC'] for the same reason orient's did.
Law 9 — red is the default, green is earned. 24 packets reading 'floor' for a field the floor never filled is a green the corpus never earned.

Law 1 — the resolver is spent on the novel. A ref that is a path had a settled answer available (component_dir's own AmbiguousComponent text already promises 'a path resolves unambiguously') and no implementation behind it, so every caller re-derived it or, here, silently gave up.

falsifier.proves_green: THREE PIECES, AND THE THIRD IS WHAT KEEPS THE FIRST TWO HONEST. (1) address.component_of resolves a PATH to its owning component — the other half of component_dir, asking the same question from the other end. THE DEEPEST ANCESTOR WINS, and that is the answer rather than a tie-break: components nest, so a file under devices/holder/machines/nested belongs to nested and holder is merely its holder. (2) floor_packet(intent_ref, root) authors constraints (every grounded component's falsifier, gates and owner, verbatim, each carrying its charter path and the field it came from) and unknowns (every ref it could NOT ground, carrying the why — 'not a component' is four distinct findings and they are told apart). bounds is NOT a candidate and never will be: what is in scope is a judgement about intent and no lookup produces it. (3) PROVENANCE FOR THOSE TWO IS DERIVED AT validate_constrain by re-running the floor over the packet's own intent_ref and comparing; a caller-supplied label that DISAGREES is refused rather than corrected. It sits at the gate because both doors a packet can leave by — the berth and the deposit — run that function.
falsifier.proves_red: RED if: (1) a packet is berthed whose provenance for constraints/unknowns was written by its sender rather than derived — the self-report restored; (2) THE DERIVED FLOOR FRACTION GOES UP WHILE THE PACKETS GET THINNER, i.e. the ceiling stopped writing its own law, ruling, ticket and memory constraints because the floor had already filled the field. This is the failure where every instrument in the system reads the damage as progress, and it is what the WATCHME exists for; (3) a floor-authored constraint names a source that does not exist on disk, or one the installed constraint_traces judge cannot resolve — a floor that invents is worse than a ceiling that invents, because it wears a measurement's provenance; (4) the 'floor' label becomes STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE for constraints — a label that can only ever take one value is a constant, not a measurement, and it blinds the dial to the thing the dial exists to see; (5) constrain grows a second opinion about where a ref points, in particular by teaching another component's judge a source spelling this module invented; (6) the change lands and the dial's readings for constrain and orient are left looking comparable when the two are now produced by different rules; (7) an oracle is consulted anywhere on this path, at fire time or at sleep — bin/cmd/determinism must keep reading this component PURE DETERMINISTIC and REFUSES GATE.
falsifier.horizon: Now, and it is done. Second rung of the build order Akien named on 2026-08-14; survey is next and inherits both halves, though NOT the survival rule — see the distinction below, because a rule copied forward without its reason is exactly how 'a tool holds no state' reached eight charters.

chart_notes.orient: The code is at cairn/devices/builder/machines/constrain/constrain.py: _resolve_ref handles both ref shapes and names the four failure reasons, _charter_constraints emits one constraint per bounding field, floor_packet authors, FLOOR_AUTHORED names the two, _survived is the two-sided rule, measured_provenance re-runs the floor, refuse_misdeclared_floor_provenance is the refusal, and validate_constrain is the gate both doors run. The new primitive is component_of in cairn/tools/base/address.py, beside component_dir. Proofs: 16 teeth at the machine, one at address's own proof for the deepest-owner rule. The reading instrument is skills/chart/dial.py. The evidence is 41 berthed constrain packets and 45 orient packets under ~/.cairn/devices/chart/0/packets/.
chart_notes.constrain: IN: constrain, component_of, their proofs, constrain's charter, one probe. OUT and stated: survey and the five nexi after it (Akien's order is one at a time, ONCE THEY WORK); the dial's own code; anything on hex.local; the six remaining charters of a-charter-may-not-assert-a-file-that-is-not-there; and any widening of what the floor authors — bounds stays the ceiling's forever.
chart_notes.validate: The tooth a hollow build fails runs in TWO directions, and the second is the one mirroring orient would have missed. FORWARD: berth a packet declaring constraints: floor for a list the floor did not produce, and require refusal — a hollow build accepts the sender's dict, which is today's 24 packets. BACKWARD: take a packet the floor's answer genuinely survived into and require the label to read 'floor'. A build whose rule is set equality passes the first and fails the second while looking correct, because 'nothing ever earns it' and 'nothing ever forges it' are the same observation from one side. Run by hand against the live rule: honest -> floor 17/17, drop a floor constraint -> claude 17/17, forge a charter-kind one -> claude 17/17, add a ticket-kind one -> still floor.
